payload.title: Santorini vs Mykonos for Your Wedding
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, often with parents contributing, who have narrowed Greece down to two islands and keep going back and forth between Santorini and Mykonos. They want the two compared on the same terms (setting, venue types, ceremony options, guest experience, getting there, season and paperwork) so they can choose one island with confidence and move on to venues.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation at /wonderland-concierge so an advisor can test the couple's chosen island against their dates, guest count and ceremony type.
payload.angle: Page-one results for Santorini versus Mykonos either crown a winner or lean on clichés (sunsets for one, parties for the other). This is a side-by-side decision guide, not a ranking: the two islands compared on the same seven terms, in the same order, with the same honesty. Santorini is the caldera and its cliff-top villages; Mykonos is beaches, bays and Mykonos Town. Venue examples are drawn only from venues already verified in our Santorini and Mykonos venue guides, kept short and linked through. Guest experience is described as official tourism sources describe each island's culture, not party stereotypes. Getting there names both airports and ports from official sources only. Season uses the HNMS Naxos station (the nearest listed station to both islands, so the same figures apply, labelled as such) with Smartraveller heat, wildfire and ferry and wind advice, and no best month. The legal steps are the same Greek civil steps for both, as at November 2026. It ends with 'which suits you' scenarios, so the reader leaves with a choice, not a verdict.
must_include: Intro with a direct answer in the first 100 words: both islands suit a luxury wedding; Santorini is caldera and cliff-top views, Mykonos is beaches, bays and Mykonos Town; the right one depends on setting, ceremony type, guest experience and pace. Link /destinations/europe/greece.

At a glance: mobile-friendly comparison table, Santorini and Mykonos as columns, rows for setting and feel, venue types, ceremony types venues state, guest experience and pace, getting there, season, legal steps. No figures that are not sourced; no prices.
Setting and feel: caldera and cliff-top views versus beaches and Mykonos Town, only as official tourism sources describe them.

Venue types and examples: 2 to 4 named example venues per island, taken only from venues already verified in /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding-venues and /destination-weddings/mykonos-wedding-venues and described no further than those finals state; short, then link both venue guides. This section carries the ONLY Advisor line in the body (brand-facts claims only), plus a link to /wonderland-concierge.
Ceremony types as venues state them (for example terrace, chapel, winery, beach-side) for each island; nothing a venue does not state.
Guest experience and pace: as official tourism sources (Visit Greece and similar) describe each island's culture, villages and food; no party stereotypes.
Getting there: both islands' airports and ports from official sources only (airport operator, port, Visit Greece); Smartraveller ferry advice; no transfers or drive times.
Season: HNMS Naxos station averages, labelled as the nearest listed station to both islands so the same figures apply; Smartraveller heat, wildfire and ferry and wind advice; no 'best month'.

Legal in brief, as at November 2026, dated once: the same Greek civil steps for both islands; Municipality of Thira versus Municipality of Mykonos only as an official page sourced live states, else 'check with the municipality and the embassy, including any fees'; Embassy Athens and Smartraveller; link /expert-advice/greek-wedding-traditions once. Nothing on church or religious paperwork.

Which suits you: 4 to 6 short scenarios (for example a cliff-top ceremony with a view, a beach-side weekend, guests who want villages and walking, a weekend centred on Mykonos Town), each pointing to one island without calling either 'best'.

FAQ (4 to 6): Is Santorini or Mykonos better for a wedding (answered as 'it depends on', no verdict)? Can we marry legally on either island? How do guests get to each island? When can we marry on each island? Can we do both islands in one trip (only if official ferry sources support it, else drop)?

Close: the one Advisor line from brand-facts.md (never the definition line or its closing phrase). Links: /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding, /destination-weddings/mykonos-wedding, /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding-venues, /destination-weddings/mykonos-wedding-venues (all drafts), /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues, /expert-advice/greek-wedding-traditions (once), /wonderland-concierge (anchor names 'Wedded Concierge'), /magazine as the magnet. UTMs utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-or-mykonos-wedding&utm_content=primary|secondary|magnet|closing on /wonderland-concierge and /magazine only.
avoid: Any price, fee, minimum spend or amount; 'free'; any capacity, distance, flight or drive time, or transfer arrangement.
'Best', 'winner' or ranking language; 'best month'; declaring one island better.
Party-island or crowd stereotypes; guest-experience claims not from an official tourism source.
Venue names other than those already verified in the two sister venue guides; any other vendor names; venue contact or business details (defer to the venue guides and the Advisor).
Restating the sister guides at length: venue-list intent belongs to the venue guides, planning-step intent to the island planning guides.
Research talk in copy ('on its own site', what we could or could not confirm); per-line source credits; hedge stacking; linking a source more than once.
Competitor wedding sites, directories, planner blogs, booking or review sites, Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording or images.

Wedded Privileges; Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; more than one Advisor line in the body besides the close; the Wedded Advisor definition line in brand-facts.md and the phrase 'last dance'; 'Wonderland Concierge' as anchor text; church or religious paperwork detail.
Clichés (fairytale, dream day, breathtaking), exclamation marks, keywords pasted in headings, em dashes, US spelling.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding; images other than placeholders.
payload.cannibalisation_check: None found for the 'vs/or' comparison intent: no URL in content-system/seo/link-map.csv targets 'santorini or mykonos wedding' or 'santorini vs mykonos'. Sisters own their head terms: /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding (santorini wedding, planning), /destination-weddings/mykonos-wedding (mykonos wedding, planning), /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding-venues and /destination-weddings/mykonos-wedding-venues (venue lists), all drafts. This post owns the comparison intent only, keeps venues to short examples and links all four. /destinations/europe/greece is the hub; /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues is the parent venues guide; /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding-packages and /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages are package intent and not needed. Legacy /7-must-see-santorini-destination-wedding-venues not linked (venues guide replaces it). SEO to check rankings for 'santorini or mykonos wedding' and variants (santorini vs mykonos wedding, mykonos or santorini for wedding, santorini vs mykonos).
